en:
I've completed the health
checkups for Heath and
Jeanne, and as Valka
suspected, neither shows any
effects from the petrification
virus.
That's great! But how does\nthat work?

My hypothesis is that while
they are infected, their bodies
have adapted to the state of
infection.

However, there are no
significant differences when
compared to the Captain's
genetic structure, so we'll have
to conduct further research to
identify the root cause.

Even on the home planet of
Raza, there are no reports of
humans becoming completely
petrified. In most cases, slight
symptoms appear and then
vanish without incident.
Still, we can't let our guard\ndown as long as the full nature\nof the virus remains unknown.

...And yet, it's frustrating that
we can't even settle down to
implement planet-wide
countermeasures right now.
Why not?
Currently, Raza and Ober are\nin a state of ceasefire across\nall sectors.

However, the leadership of the
Raza Space Force, who should
be navigating our future
relations, have all gone missing.
Apparently, they vanished at\nsome point during the chaos of\nthat fleet battle.
My, how unsettling...
We defeated Asmodeus and\nEve is back, but there are still\nso many things we don't know...
Rekoro, is Eve still not waking\nup?
Fortunately, her condition is\nstable, but there are no signs\nof her waking.
I see...

Verda, Valka, and Henri are
apparently administering a
serum using biological samples
from Asmodeus, but the
results have been
underwhelming.
While there are no signs of\npetrification, a full recovery will\nlikely take some time.

I know Verda and Henri; they
could never just ignore a
disease that consumes entire
planets.
I just hope the damage doesn't\nspread any further... oh.
Good work, Verda. Are you\nokay? You look exhausted...

Hmm... Tika, you're right. I might
have pushed myself a bit too
hard. Eve's condition just isn't
improving as quickly as I'd
hoped...
Sit down here. Do you want\nsomething warm to drink?
My apologies... By the way,\nCoro, how long do you plan on\nstaying dressed like that?

I'd love to repair myself, but
right now every bit of material
refining must be dedicated to
creating the serum...

Under these circumstances, it's
simply impossible to recreate
my complete, perfect, and
marvelous body.

Since my own performance
depends on the ship's
capabilities, I think I'll have to
stay like this until everything
settles down.
It's quite depressing that even\nyou seem to be in bad shape.
Well, if you're fine with it...\nthen... that's... fine...
Sister Verda!?
Ah, s-sorry, Tika. I don't know\nwhat's happening... my knees\njust gave out...
Ms. Verda! ...Oh no! She has a\nterrible fever!
...Sorry, Tika... I feel a bit...\nlightheaded...

Stay with me, Sister Verda!
Let's go to the infirmary! I'll
carry you on my back, so just
hold on!
Wait! Tika!! Stop!! Get away\nfrom Verda!!
Huh? W-what!?
...Was I too late...!!
Coro! Call Mastima and the\nCaptain! Then, get Valka and\nHenri away from Eve! Hurry!!
...Rekoro, don't tell me I'm...
...You're infected.
Whaaat!?
N-no way...!

Verda Kleiman is infected with
the petrification virus! There is
a high probability that Tika is
infected as well since she was
in contact!
This is an emergency! Summon\nLambda! Coro! Hurry!
Y-yessssss!!
...Forgive me... Tika... I thought I\nwas being careful...
Don't talk...! I'm still fine! Let's\nget to the infirmary, just hold\non tight.
Forgive me... Haha, I suppose\nthis is what they call the tables\nbeing turned.

...Sister Verda. It's okay... This
disease has been known for a
long time... I know you'll get
better...!
I have just confirmed that Tika,\nRicardo, Karlyn, and Giverese\nare also infected...
...What are we supposed to do\nabout this...?
Face reality. Crying won't help.

...The infectivity of this virus is
abnormal. Could it have
become even more vicious than
it was during the time on
Planet Roak that the captains
mentioned?

Now that you mention it... my
father's comrades said they
couldn't identify the route of
infection when they fell ill...

It's possible that the
petrification disease Coro
knows about and the one I
know about are different types.
Is there a possibility that Givel\nwas infected from the start?

Even though he was captured,
he was with Asmodeus;
perhaps he had a longer
incubation period due to
genetic differences...

If that were the case, Valka
should have detected it the
moment he was brought
aboard the Overman.

I have evacuated Euwin, Welch,
and Lavarnia to the Overman,
as I could definitively confirm
they are not infected.

As for Heath and Jeanne, they
are currently waiting in the
infirmary since they are
infected.

Henri has not shown
symptoms, but since he was
present for Eve's examination
from the beginning, there is a
suspicion of incubation.
Kevin is looking after everyone\nfor now, but...

In that case, it would mean it's
purely a coincidence that we
haven't developed symptoms
yet.

Exactly. Especially for you,
Captain; I can't rule out the
possibility that you're in the
incubation period, just like
Henri.
What's the status of the serum\ndevelopment?
The prototype we've created so far has not been effective against Lady Eve...

en:
...Furthermore, we'll need
separate serums tailored for
Daftine, Daftes, Levarance, and
Earthlings.
As for Lady Eve and Givel, we haven't even been able to identify their genetic structures.

en: Can't we detect a serum or\nantibodies from the bodies of\nRaza like Heath and Jeanne?
It seems their bodies don't\nactually possess antigens\nagainst the virus.

Instead, it appears their bodies
have adapted to the virus's
presence, rendering it
harmless.

Even if we could analyze that
mechanism, there's simply no
time to apply it to everyone on
this ship.
We're completely boxed in,\nthen.

Could we ask Ober for their
cooperation? Asmodeus had
already established the
technology to mass-produce
this virus and integrate it into
weapons.

That means Ober should have
a wealth of know-how
regarding how to handle the
virus.

And how do you plan to get
them to hand it over? We're
still outsiders, and most of
Raza's leadership capable of
negotiating a ceasefire have
gone missing.

Jeanne Marswest isn't in a
position of power where she'd
be entrusted with all the
negotiations.

Besides, if we make a careless
move and trigger a
petrification pandemic in Ober,
that'll be the end of us for
sure.
Then what are we supposed to\ndo?! We're completely out of\noptions here!
Please calm down, Valka! This\nis no time to be fighting...

Our only choice is to continue
our research steadily. The
silver lining is that this is not a
fatal disease.

Kevin, Valka, and I―since we
aren't at risk of infection―will
take the lead and focus on the
research.

We can rely on Euwin, Welch,
and Lavarnia for external
affairs, such as securing
supplies.
I guess... that's all we can do.

At this rate, we don't know
when the Captain might show
symptoms. We have to start
with what we can... Captain.
Captain!? What's wrong?
C-C-C-C-Captainnnnn!?
Damn it... it's happened!
Captain! Stay with us!
Captain! Please, pull yourself\ntogether, Captain!!

I can't believe this... To think
the day would come where the
Captain and Eve both catch
the same illness and end up
bedridden together... haha...

Don't lose heart. For now, the
most important thing is to get
some rest. Please leave
everything else to us.
Eve's condition seems to have\nstabilized for now, and she is\nsleeping soundly.

Mmm... sorry, but could you
keep an eye on Valka so she
doesn't start crying? She must
be exhausted.
...It's okay. Valka is holding up.
I see... she's grown strong...\nWait, is it presumptuous of me\nto say that?
Now, please get some sleep.\nWe'll be back later.
Hey, Captain, Coro.

Ever since Eve disappeared,
Tika and Mastima have been
fighting a lot, haven't they?
Mastima always suspected Eve
was plotting something...
Now that you mention it, that's\ntrue.

Come to think of it, I feel like
Mastima has been suspicious
of Eve ever since they were in
Daftine...

It's true that the conflict in
Daftine over the Summoning
Gems was full of unnatural
occurrences.
Eve possesses the same power\nas Givel.

In that case, it isn't entirely
unnatural to think there is
some kind of connection
between the two...
But... I simply couldn't believe\nthat Eve was such a\ncalculating, malicious person...
It couldn't be... Back then,\nEve...!

You're talking about when the
captain contracted Pyre
Disease at the Levarance
space station, aren't you,
Verda?
...So, you remember that time\nas well, Coro?
How could I forget? A cure for\nPyre Disease hadn't even been\nestablished yet.
And yet, the captain\nrecovered.
I could only conclude that Eve's\nsigil arts had made it happen.

If Eve were a villain like Givel
and only kept the captain alive
because they were useful... I
don't think she would have
looked so desperate.
If she had been confident in\nher ability to save the captain...

It would have been far more
effective to calm the chaos
and act composed if she
wanted people to trust her...
Everyone was so desperate\nback then.

True... Someone like Eve, who
would go to such irrational
lengths just to save her
comrades... she couldn't
possibly be a villain.
You're right... I believe so too.
*Sigh*... I've talked too much.\nI'm going to sleep for a bit.
All right. Please get some good\nrest.
...Traveling the Sea of Stars...\nthere really is never a dull\nmoment.
Haaah!
I won't let you get away!
Take this! And this! Get\ncrushed, you!! Daaaaah!
Alright... looks like that took\ncare of most of them.

I believe the number we
defeated is roughly consistent
with the projections from the
Bazaar Council.
Hmph!
Welch seems quite worked up.

Even when looking at the Gem
mining machines in the mine,
there was no reaction. It's a
serious condition.
She's frustrated because her\nfriends are sick and she can't\neven go visit them.
But the Stardust Bazaar has\nbeen helped a lot by Welch and\nthe others.

Thanks to everyone, we've
mostly confirmed the damage
from when Raza and Ober
attacked. My dad is happy too.
I understand that feeling of\nrestlessness.

I understand. If I were facing
the leadership who abandoned
their posts during a planetary
crisis, I'd be tempted to take
their heads myself.

Furthermore, even if they've
been neutralized, we don't
know how the petrification
virus in Heath and me would
affect the residents of the
Ober system.

Because of that, we cannot
even land at the Bazaar. We
are truly grateful for the help
of Euwin, Welch, and Lavarnia.

Seriously, the big picture
should be improving, but
nothing feels right. I get why
people want to lash out.

Both Raza's and Ober's armies
are in total shambles. Who
knows what's going to happen
to the Azurite system now?

Overthinking is as bad as doing
nothing. For now, I suppose we
have no choice but to stay
here in this remote asteroid
belt and focus on pest
control...
Hm?
What is it, Boss?

Speak of the devil. We have a
transmission from Coro. He
wants everyone to return to
the ship.
I wonder what happened? I\nhope it's not bad news...
I don't know if this helps, but it\nseems they are about to leave\nthe Stardust Bazaar.
Apparently, Eve has woken up.
What!?
Are you serious!?
Yes. On Eve's orders, they are\ngoing to remove our\npetrification disease.
They say the destination is\nPlanet Lazuli.
O shining stars... become the\nlight... that guides him...
Nnh... ah...
...What the hell happened?
What on earth happened... to\nthe petrification virus...?

It's all gone. I used the Gate of
Urza to amplify the power of
the Gems and my own, and
then I repaired it.
How is such a thing possible? I\nassume you can provide an\nexplanation.
I know. I'll tell you everything...\nright, Givel?
...Do as you please.
Miss Eve... could it be that your\nmemories...
...Yeah. To be honest, I lost\nmost of them back in Daftine.
So you admit it.
That's right. I knew Givel. Back\nthen, I let him escape.

Givel and I have always
disagreed on things... and in
the end, I realized we could
never understand each other.
But...
...I couldn't bring myself to kill\nhim.

...That was when I met Heath.
Heath, who possesses the
same Earthling genes as the
Captain.

I realized then. The reason
Givel and I disagreed so
fundamentally... was because
Heath's Earth was the cause of
it all.
Givel said your goal was to\ndestroy Raza. I bet that's not\nexactly what you meant, either.

That might not be entirely
wrong. More than anyone, I
wanted Raza to return to
where it belongs.
Because Raza... Earth... has\nvanished from the universe.
Gone...? Are you saying that\nAnother Earth has warped\naway from the Solar System?
How does Eve know about\nthis? Did she see it in the Urza\nSystem?
No. I... I've known about it from\nthe very beginning.
...From the beginning? What do\nyou mean by "the beginning"?\nWhat is this all about?

The beginning. Ever since the
Earth where Kevin's parents
were born became the planet
Raza...
B-but that was hundreds of\nyears ago!

Being long-lived isn't
necessarily strange. Some of
us, like me and Mastima, can
live many times longer than a
normal Human in our own flesh.
Henri, Kevin, and even Valka\nhave lived for a long time\nthanks to technology. But...
The fact that planet Raza was once Earth shouldn't be a part of this universe... To have known that from the start... Lady Eve, who exactly are you?

en: When you study Symbols for a\nlong time, you occasionally run\ninto that same question.

No, not even Symbols, but
simpler things like physics and
chemistry. Things that should
have existed and formed
naturally.
...I can feel the will of someone\nwho created them.
A "god," then?
Now that's a cruel joke.\nEspecially coming from you.

The Demon Realm and Demon
Lords exist. It wouldn't be
unnatural if an opposing force
existed somewhere in the
universe.
Can you actually bring yourself\nto believe in something like a\n"god," Mastima?

God is a concept that
intelligent life across the
universe has sought eternally.
If scientific evidence can prove
its existence, I would be more
than willing to accept it.

...I see. Unfortunately, I've
never seen a god either.
Though I've known plenty of
arrogant types who think they
are one.
Evelysse, what exactly were\nyou trying to achieve here in\nthe Azurite system?

...I wanted to prevent a
calamity that might strike this
universe in the distant future.
That... calamity.
...What?

After hearing what Tika and
Ricardo had to say... I thought
that perhaps the existence of
a planet that shouldn't be
here... the fact that "two of the
same planet" exist in this
universe...
...might have triggered the\ncrisis, so I wanted to correct it.

...Don't be ridiculous. Even if
that were true, the Exorciser
was meant to be the tool to fix
it.
That failed, which is why you\nlost to us as Daftine. Did you\nforget?

Givel and I were completely at
odds over what to do about
the Earth that vanished from
the universe.

Part of the reason we
disagreed was that we didn't
know why the other Earth had
disappeared.

I believed that we had to
return the vanished Earth to
its original place, no matter
what. But Givel...

If it was meant to vanish, then
that is the correct history for
that planet. To distort that
would be unacceptable.

...It sounds as if you think you
have the right to decide the
life or death of an entire
planet.
But based on what we've\nheard, that is exactly what\nthey are saying.

Talking as if they held a single
planet, or the entire universe,
in the palm of their hand... truly
just "god-complex show-offs."
That's right! I remember Eve\nbringing a planet back to life.
Planet Berbent. Didn't Eve do\nsomething to the entire dying\nplanet back then?
...That brings back memories. I\nremember that happening.
Berbent... the planet that was\non the brink of destruction\nbecause of the Pulse Tower.
That's right. Eve used a\nmysterious Symbol Art just\nonce on that planet.

I don't know what kind of
power was at work, but a
single person's Symbol Art
stopped an earthquake that
was shaking the entire surface
of the planet...
...It brings back memories. I\nremember that happening.
It's true that I hadn't recovered\nall of my memories back then.

en:
Perhaps that's why the
appearance of the Thornite felt
like the universe was telling me
I was wrong,

Perhaps that's why the
appearance of Thornite felt like
the universe telling me I was
wrong.
Since I couldn't remember the\ntruth, Thornite appeared to me\nas a terrifying existence.

After that, Thornite appeared
every time I interfered with a
planet, continuing to tell me
that I was wrong.
Not until I met Heath.

Not until I saw the people
desperately fighting to survive
on the current Earth... no, on
planet Raza.
Not until I saw the people\nfighting so hard to survive on\ncurrent Earth... no, Planet Raza.
Ah, I realized then that Givel\nwas right all along.

After seeing the history of
Planet Raza through the Gate
of Urza... I felt that I had to
apologize.
That's why... I looked for Givel.\nBut by then, he was already...
Had he been captured by\nAsmodeus?
...Yes.
...I'm totally lost here. Can you\njust clear things up for me?
What exactly is the relationship\nbetween Eve and Givel?
Givel is... my younger brother.
Oh.
Oh.
Oh.
My little\nbrotherrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr!!?
...Now that you mention it, they\ndo have a similar vibe.
N-no, but that's... Wait, WHAT!?\nSiblings!?
This is even more shocking\nthan when we found out Tika\nand Ricardo were siblings...
I'd like to say don't lump us\ntogether, but... I can see it...
...If you're joking, that's in very\nbad taste.
It's the truth. As everyone\nknows, their personalities are\ncompletely different, though.

I feel like there's something
much more important to worry
about than their personalities
in this situation...

However, if she was trying to
save her brother, it would be
understandable why she had
no choice but to obey
Asmodeus, who was holding
him hostage.
But why did you continue to\nobey Asmodeus even after we\nhad Giverese in our custody?

He likely knew that if he lost
the means to summon the
Phantom, Asmodeus would
spread the petrification
disease across Raza.
What?
At the time, all I knew was that\nit was some kind of terrifying\nvirus.
I can control the Phantom, but\na virus is a different story.
That's why I had no choice but\nto stay with him to prevent him\nfrom using the virus.
In the end... it was all for\nnothing.

After traveling through the
Azurite system, I realized that I
couldn't let Raza―who had
started walking a new path―be
sent back to the original Earth.
...But there were many people\nin Raza who didn't feel the\nsame way.
Could that be related to the\nRaza leadership who are\ncurrently missing?
The reason I summoned\nAsmodeus was...

Because Ober desired a strong
leader who could lead Raza to
victory and seize control of the
Azurite system.

At the time, I needed to build
up my forces so I could return
to Daftine, where I had
succeeded in creating the rift.
But...

And while you were weakened,
Asmodeus, whom you
summoned, rebelled against
you.

...Precisely. Ever since the
current civilization was
established, there have always
been factions within Raza that
sought to return Earth to
where it truly belonged.

Asmodeus already had a
strong desire to oppose
humanity, so he conspired with
those who wanted to return
Raza to the original form and
location of Earth.

...By using both the Phantom
fleet and the petrification virus
to corner Raza, he intended to
create a justification for
returning to the original Earth.

...I don't necessarily deny the
ideology of longing for the
original Earth. My foster
parents are certainly
responsible for the disasters
that struck the world after the
warp.
But what exactly do they plan\nto do by actually going back to\nthe Earth of that era?

If we return to a time when
people across the planet were
at each other's throats and
energy was depleted, the
humanity that managed to
survive will only face extinction
again...!

...Maybe they didn't think that
far ahead. I think the desire to
return to their original form
just took precedence over
everything else.

Perhaps they hoped that if
they just changed the
situation, a paradise would
naturally appear. ...I'm just
guessing, though.

But wait, does that mean
everyone who's missing right
now... all hold those kinds of
dangerous beliefs!?

That's insane! They're trying to
throw away all our current
prosperity just to realize some
pointless fact that this place
used to be Earth!
That's right. I was the same\nway...

...But I won't let that happen
ever again... and I won't forgive
anyone who tries to make it
happen.

You're activating the Urza
System quite easily. I had such
a hard time with it. What is this
footage?
This is a fleet from the Raza\nSpace Force.

Just a bunch of fools
obsessed with the same ideas
as me. I think they took
advantage of the ceasefire to
come and raid the Urza
System.
Boss! Look at that! No way, is\nthat...!

...That is... the
Commander-in-Chief of the
Raza Home World Defense
Force.

I know this guy. Until last year,
he was the Plenipotentiary
Ambassador at the Raza
Embassy in the Bazaar.
What is that... those purple\ncrystal-like things beside\nthem...?
It's Grigori... fragments of\nGrigori... there's no mistake!

That's Grigori? The thing
Bacchus D79 and the others
supposedly drove out of
space...?

Exactly, and it's bad. The
people in the footage have
been completely consumed by
Grigori!
Grigori parasitizes living\norganisms to amplify and\nweaponize their desires!

...So Raza's catastrophic
ideology of returning to Earth
was the result of being
infected by this Grigori!
It is true that Grigori may have\ntriggered this situation.

Even so, there was
undoubtedly a desire within
their hearts that Grigori could
exploit.
A desire to return to Earth, to\ntheir homeland, no matter the\ncost...

Once again, the people of Raza
sought power... Instead of
trying to reach it through their
own strength, they mistook a
sweet temptation for salvation.
The enemy fleet has deployed\nabove Planet Lazuli! Abnormal\nenergy reactions confirmed!

...You can tell just by looking.
Those people in the footage...
that's the reaction of those
infected by Grigori...

Even though it's happening far
away, the noise is grating and
making me sick. The stench of
the Crest is enough to blow my
nose off.
Humans... turned into that... Is\nthis really happening right\nnow!?

There's no point in shaking now
that you can see it. Steel
yourself; we've come too far to
have any other choice.
...You're right. We can't let\nthings like that exist forever.\nReady, Givel?

They obstruct the activities of
the Exorciser and distort the
proper state of the universe.
They are targets to be
eliminated.
...Small, pitiful, boring fragments\nof will, possessed by the desire\nto seek their homeland...

It was proven long ago that
something like Grigori has no
influence whatsoever on the
legitimate evolution of this
universe.

en: ...I will eliminate them. For the\nsake of the universe's future.
Abnormal energy reaction\ndescending!
Let 'em come!! I'll never forgive\nanyone who threatens my\nhome... the Azurite system!
Those possessed by Grigori\ncan never return to the way\nthey were, can they?
I don't know how human they\never were...

Because they hid their pathetic
little ambitions, countless
people died who shouldn't
have.
I can't bring myself to feel\nsorry for them.
Is it really over now? The war\nin the Azurite system, and\nEve's struggle...?
No, there is still something\nimportant left to do.

To ensure that nuisances like
Grigori and Thornite never
disturb the peace of those
living in this universe again...
We must make sure the people\nof Raza and Ober cannot\napproach this Urza System.

Captain! Emergency! Fleets
from both the Raza Space
Force and the Ober Space
Force are approaching Lazuli!
What!? Why!?

The war isn't over yet. They
probably saw the Grigori fleet
approaching Lazuli and mistook
it for the enemy closing in.
Shall we intercept them? I can\ntake command of the bridge if\nyou wish.
It's fine. This was all part of\nthe plan.

I intentionally had the Overman
follow behind us, using an
illness as an excuse, so they
would be easier to detect.
...What? What do you mean by\nthat?
There is nothing on this planet\nthat would benefit either Raza\nor Ober.

On the contrary, I want them
to return home with the
knowledge that approaching
this place is dangerous.

Especially for the fleets that
fought at Raza's final line of
defense; they will understand
that terror all too well.
...O sparkling stars.
Become the beacon that\nguides them.
Karnas, Accura, Elemia, Valena,\nDandelion... and another\nKarnas...
Charles de Gaulle, Diplo,\nAquariel... and...
Go... protect the future of the\nAzurite system... you phantom\nfleets...

Ensure that people are never
plagued by a power that
denies the very existence of
life...!
Phantoms that shouldn't exist\nin this universe... the Phantom\nFleet, huh...
Why not just let this fleet\ndestroy the Urza System?
